name: Kansas

agency.name: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks

overview: KDWP runs separate online draws: the nonresident deer draw in April (whitetail permits by deer management unit, plus a Mule Deer Stamp draw), resident firearm either-species deer, antelope and elk draws in May-June, and the nonresident and Unit 4 spring turkey draws in January-February. Deer, antelope and turkey draws use preference points (applicants with more points are drawn first) and the elk draw uses bonus points; unsuccessful applicants earn a point and points can be bought instead of applying; deer, antelope and elk points are reset after five years without an application or point purchase. Most resident deer permits, resident spring turkey permits outside Unit 4 and all archery antelope permits are sold over the counter.

species.drawSystemSummary: Nonresident White-tailed Deer (either-sex) permits are issued only through KDWP's April lottery (nonresident antlerless-only and hunt-own-land permits are sold over the counter): each applicant picks one deer management unit (plus one adjacent unit to also hunt) and a season (archery, muzzleloader or firearm), and applicants with more preference points are drawn first. Unsuccessful applicants receive a preference point, and a point can be bought instead of applying. Resident whitetail permits are sold over the counter.
species.residentNote: Residents buy Any-Season White-tailed Deer, Archery Either-Species/Either-Sex and Muzzleloader Either-Species/Either-Sex permits over the counter (Aug. 5-Dec. 31); the only resident deer draw is the Firearm Either-Species/Either-Sex permit (see mule deer).
species.nonresidentNote: Apply online (GoOutdoorsKS) during the April application period; a nonresident hunting license is required at the time of application. Group applications (up to 5, same unit and weapon) are drawn at the lowest preference point in the group. Preference points are reset to zero if no application or point purchase is made in 5 consecutive years. The $475 permit includes a nonrefundable $25 application fee; the rest is charged only if drawn.
species.otcSummary: Residents: Any-Season White-tailed, Archery and Muzzleloader Either-Species/Either-Sex, Hunt-Own-Land and Whitetail Antlerless-Only permits over the counter. Nonresidents: up to 10 Whitetail Antlerless-Only permits over the counter (Aug. 5-Dec. 31), in addition to any permit drawn.

species.displayName: Mule deer (resident Either-Species/Either-Sex firearm permit; nonresident Mule Deer Stamp)
species.drawSystemSummary: Residents draw Firearm Either-Species/Either-Sex permits (valid for white-tailed or mule deer) for the West Zone (Units 1, 2, 17, 18) or East Zone (Units 3, 4, 5, 7, 16) with preference points. Nonresidents cannot draw a mule deer permit directly: a nonresident who draws an archery or muzzleloader whitetail permit in Units 1, 2, 17 or 18 and applied for the Mule Deer Stamp is entered in a separate stamp draw, where preference points do not count.
species.residentNote: Resident firearm either-species permits are draw-only (application May 12-June 12, 2026); a $10 preference point can be bought instead. Archery and muzzleloader either-species/either-sex permits (which include mule deer) are sold over the counter.
species.nonresidentNote: Apply for the Mule Deer Stamp ($150, on top of the whitetail permit) during the April nonresident application. If the stamp is drawn, the whitetail archery or muzzleloader permit converts to an either-species/either-sex permit; if not, the hunter keeps the whitetail permit.
species.otcSummary: Residents: Archery Either-Species/Either-Sex (statewide) and Muzzleloader Either-Species/Either-Sex (East or West zone) permits over the counter, Aug. 5-Dec. 31.

species.drawSystemSummary: Firearm and muzzleloader antelope permits are resident-only and drawn by unit (2, 17, 18) and weapon, with separate general and landowner/tenant allocations. Permits go first to applicants with the most preference points; if more applicants are tied at the top level than permits remain, a random drawing decides. Archery permits are over the counter.
species.residentNote: Apply May 12-June 12, 2026 (online or by phone). A point can be bought instead of applying, but not in the same year as buying an antelope permit. All points are lost once a firearm or muzzleloader permit is drawn, or after 5 years without an application.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may only buy over-the-counter archery antelope permits ($300); nonresident tenants may apply for the resident firearm draw.
species.otcSummary: Archery antelope permits over the counter for residents ($50) and nonresidents ($300).

species.drawSystemSummary: Elk hunting is limited to Kansas residents and qualifying nonresident tenants. Permits for Unit 2 and Fort Riley Subunit 2A are drawn, with one extra chance in the draw for each bonus point; active-duty military stationed at Fort Riley have their own preferential draw. Unit 3 permits and hunt-own-land permits are sold over the counter.
species.residentNote: Apply May 12-June 12, 2026; an applicant cannot apply and buy a bonus point in the same year, and points are lost when a permit is drawn or after 5 years without an application. Fort Riley any-elk permits are once in a lifetime; Fort Riley antlerless permits once every five years. KDWP does not publish per-hunt elk draw statistics; its 2024-25 Elk Harvest Report counts 2,564 Fort Riley applications or point purchases for 2024 (1,954 for 2023). KDWP's fee table calls the $10 elk point a 'Preference Point'; its elk page describes bonus points.
species.nonresidentNote: Not available to nonresidents (nonresident tenants only).
species.otcSummary: Unit 3 elk permits over the counter for residents; hunt-own-land permits over the counter in Units 2 and 3 for landowners/tenants.

species.drawSystemSummary: Nonresident spring turkey permits (Units 1, 2, 3, 5, 6; one unit per permit) are issued only through a January-February lottery, and Unit 4 spring permits are a resident and nonresident-tenant draw (375 permits, 200 reserved for landowners/tenants). Unsuccessful applicants receive a preference point; a point can be bought instead of applying.
species.residentNote: Residents buy spring permits for Units 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 over the counter; Unit 4 is draw-only. The fall season reopened in 2026 for residents only (permits over the counter from Oct. 1, 2026). Resident youth permits are valid statewide, including Unit 4.
species.nonresidentNote: Apply Jan. 13-Feb. 13, 2026 for one unit (1, 2, 3, 5 or 6); $10 application fee plus $75 permit if drawn. 9,700 nonresident permits were authorized for 2026. Nonresident youth are also subject to the draw.
species.otcSummary: Residents and nonresident tenants: spring permits for Units 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 over the counter; resident fall permits over the counter.

coverage.notes: Nonresident Whitetail Either Sex permits by deer management unit (Units 1-18). 2024-2026: quota, 1st-choice applicants, permits issued (sum of KDWP's issued-by-preference-point rows, which match KDWP's statewide totals 21,830 / 21,736 / 21,708) and the lowest point level drawn; the permits issued at each point level are in each row's note. KDWP does not publish applicants by point level, so no per-point odds are given. 2022-2023: permits authorized only (KDWP replaces its draw report every year and no copy of those years' reports survives). 2025 uses KDWP's PDF report because the 2025 web table has transcription errors in Units 4, 6, 7, 13, 17 and 18 (listed in those rows). Resident whitetail permits are over the counter (no draw).

Resident Firearm Either-Species/Either-Sex draw (West and East zones; permit valid for white-tailed or mule deer) and the nonresident Mule Deer Stamp draw by unit. 2022-2023: permits/stamps authorized only. 2024 stamp: stamps issued not published. 2025 resident rows use KDWP's PDF (the web page omits a 4-point row). 2026 East Zone applicants left empty because KDWP's published total (168) conflicts with its own categories (176).

Resident firearm and muzzleloader draw for Units 2, 17 and 18, split into KDWP's General and Landowner Tenant allocations; youth and nonresident-tenant applicant counts are given in notes because KDWP does not say which allocation they draw from. 2025 Unit 2 Firearms Landowner Tenant permits issued left empty (KDWP's point rows add to 45 against a quota of 44 and a statewide total of 156).

Unit 4 spring draw (General, Landowner/Tenant and Nonresident Tenant classes) 2023-2026 and nonresident spring draw by unit 2024-2026 (the nonresident lottery began in 2024). Per-class Unit 4 quotas and 2026 per-unit nonresident quotas are not published. No 2022 Unit 4 report was found.

KDWP does not publish elk draw statistics by hunt (quota, applicants or drawn). Its 2024-25 Elk Harvest Report gives only the total Fort Riley applications plus point purchases (2,564 for 2024; 1,954 for 2023).
